name: Elliston
reason: Town visitors stop at; tourism board names the 13.6 km Elliston Coastal Trail with cliff-top sculptures and Waterloo Bay (rules 1-2).
objection: Mostly a small village; the trail is the draw and is a separate walk if listed.

name: Port Neill
reason: Wikivoyage names it as a main stopping point on the Lincoln Highway with jetty and beach, but no specific sight (one counted source).
objection: Case for: guide-listed seaside stop. Against: nothing named to see or do; thin.

name: Minnipa
reason: Wikivoyage only lists it in the town bullets, no sight named; Pildappa Rock is the draw and is a separate candidate (rule 1/2).
objection: A Granite Country gateway town a driver passes through.

name: Penong
reason: Tourism board names the Penong Windmill Museum (around 20 restored windmills, free outdoor museum) and the town is the gateway to Cactus Beach (rules 1-2).
objection: Short stop of 15-30 min; roadside icon level.

name: Fowlers Bay
reason: Agency-named conservation park village with huge dunes and whale and sea lion watching; a place visitors go to do things (rules 1-2).
objection: Remote and the park page is generic; sources thin on specific attractions.

name: Venus Bay
reason: Parks page names Venus Bay Conservation Park and the village sits on the bay, but only one counted source and no specific sight.
objection: For: park coast, fishing, bird life. Against: tiny village, little to do for half an hour.

name: Baird Bay
reason: Wikivoyage names swimming with sea lions at Baird Bay as an Eyre highlight; the place is the bay, but access is only through the operator (rule 2).
objection: For: headline wildlife encounter. Against: it is an operator experience; the bay itself has nothing to see unaided.

name: Thevenard
reason: Port suburb of Ceduna with grain and gypsum port; no visitor source names a sight (rules 1-2).
objection: Wikivoyage Ceduna mentions it only as a port.

name: Port Kenny
reason: Tiny fishing village; the only source is the Streaky Bay jetty page and names no sight at Port Kenny (rule 1).
objection: May have a jetty and bay views, but unnamed by any visitor source.

name: Cummins
reason: Tourism board names the Cummins Mosaic Trail (self-guided public art walk through town); one counted source and a short visit.
objection: For: a named trail, free, always open. Against: small farming town, art trail is minor.

name: Louth Bay
reason: Only source is an operator experience (Louth Island tour); no place to see on its own (a tour is not a spot).
objection: Louth Island access could be a place, but it is private/operator only.

name: Yalata
reason: Aboriginal community on the Eyre Highway; the only source is a roadhouse animal-crossing sign. Access to community land is restricted, no visitor sight named.
objection: The cultural tourism offering exists but is not shown by the source.

name: Nullarbor Roadhouse
reason: Southaustralia.com page did not name it; an iconic Nullarbor fuel stop but a roadhouse is a business (rule 2). Needs a second source.
objection: For: marks the Nullarbor crossing and near the cliffs. Against: plain roadhouse/shop.

name: Border Village
reason: Roadside icon (the Big Kangaroo at the WA border and quarantine point); southaustralia.com did not name it, so only the known roadside-icon case.
objection: For: quirky roadside icon travellers photograph. Against: a roadhouse with one statue, ten-minute stop, source unconfirmed.

name: Nundroo
reason: Roadhouse locality; no visitor source names anything to see (rules 1-2).
objection: A fuel stop on the Eyre Highway.

name: Koppio
reason: Southaustralia.com page does not name Koppio; Koppio Smithy Museum is a small volunteer museum with no counted source (rule 1).
objection: A museum is a legitimate stop if a source named it; could be re-judged with one.

name: Memory Cove
reason: Two counted sources (NPWS and tourism board): a secluded white-sand bay with lookouts, open by booking (15 vehicles a day), a distinct place in Lincoln National Park (rules 1-3).
objection: Part of Lincoln National Park and gated by permit, key and deposit.

name: Stamford Hill
reason: Wikivoyage and parks page name the 1.6 km return walk to the Flinders monument with views over the town and beaches (rules 1-3).
objection: A short walk inside Lincoln National Park; Lincoln NP may cover it.

name: Cape Donington
reason: Wikivoyage names the lighthouse, rocks, wildlife and views to Donington Island; a named headland (rules 1-3).
objection: Part of Lincoln National Park and one counted source.

name: September Beach
reason: Only the parks page lists it as a campground beach in Lincoln National Park; no visitor sight beyond the park (part of a larger spot).
objection: A named beach and second-tier beaches are kept elsewhere.

name: Spalding Cove
reason: Parks-page campground cove in Lincoln National Park; one source, no distinct draw beyond the park (rule 3).
objection: Sheltered swimming is a real activity; campground-based.

name: Surfleet Cove
reason: Parks-page campground cove in Lincoln National Park; one source, no distinct draw beyond the park (rule 3).
objection: The parks page does name it; neighbour of Spalding Cove.

name: Sleaford Bay
reason: Parks page names the surf beach and whale watching on the Lincoln NP south coast near the Sleaford dunes; one counted source.
objection: For: surf beach, whales, dunes. Against: 4WD/campground area inside the park.

name: Sleaford Mere
reason: No counted source found (parks page fetched without any visitor content); saline lake with bird life only (rule 1).
objection: Conservation park with birdlife; may have a source I could not reach.

name: Whalers Way
reason: Wikivoyage describes the 15 km coastal drive on private land (permit $30) with cliffs, blowholes, seals and sea lions; open to the public by permit (rules 1-3).
objection: Permit and private land; Cape Wiles is part of it.

name: Cape Wiles
reason: duplicate of Whalers Way: headland on the Whalers Way coast, no counted source.
objection: Could be a lookout in its own right.

name: Fishery Bay
reason: Tourism board names the iconic surf beach (surf reserve since 2024) with the old whaling station remains; second-tier beach (rules 1-3).
objection: Surf beach with no facilities other than a car park; one counted source.

name: Fishery Bay Whaling Station
reason: duplicate of Fishery Bay: the remains lie on the same beach and share the same source.
objection: A separate heritage feature to a heritage visitor.

name: Mikkira Station
reason: Koala sanctuary on a working farm with wild koalas; the only source is an operator tour page (the sanctuary is open to the public), one source.
objection: For: reliable wild koalas. Against: source is a tour listing, business-run.

name: Boston Bay
reason: Harbour of Port Lincoln; the only source is the Lincoln NP page, and the bay is the town foreshore (no distinct visit; Port Lincoln covers it).
objection: Largest natural harbour in Australia is a recognised feature.

name: Axel Stenross Maritime Museum
reason: Tourism board lists a boatbuilding heritage museum, open to the public ($10 adult); one counted source and small volunteer museum.
objection: For: genuine museum with harbour views. Against: local museum, one source.

name: Port Lincoln Railway Museum
reason: Tourism board lists the museum in the heritage station building with rolling stock; open to the public, one source.
objection: For: open museum with displays. Against: small volunteer museum, one source.

name: Port Lincoln Old Mill
reason: Tourism board: 1846 mill, oldest standing structure in Port Lincoln, now a lookout tower with views; one source and a short visit.
objection: For: climbable lookout with history. Against: short stop; open access uncertain.

name: Winter Hill Lookout
reason: Tourism board describes a panoramic lookout over Boston Bay and Lincoln NP just outside Port Lincoln; one source, short visit.
objection: For: the town viewpoint. Against: a 10-minute lookout.

name: Flinders and Freycinet Lookout
reason: Short lookout and interpretive site; a minor roadside pull-out with one source (rule 3).
objection: Interpretive panels give some history.

name: Mighty Mulloway Sculpture
reason: Quirky roadside icon: bronze fish statue in Port Lincoln named by the tourism board; a roadside icon but a very short stop.
objection: For: photographed civic icon. Against: a ten-minute photo stop.

name: Matthew Flinders and Trim Statue
reason: Minor statue/memorial; a short look (rule 3).
objection: Cute landmark of explorer and cat.

name: Port Lincoln Street Art Trail
reason: Tourism board lists a town street-art walk; free, always there, one source.
objection: For: walkable trail of murals. Against: minor and a town attraction.

name: Parnkalla Trail
reason: Tourism board describes a coastal trail along Boston Bay from the town centre to Lincoln National Park with lookouts and wildlife; one source.
objection: For: named trail. Against: shared-use path and one source.

name: Cape Bauer Loop Coastal Scenic Drive
reason: Tourism board names stops on the loop: Hallys Beach lookout, Whistling Rocks and Blowholes, Cape Bauer cliffs and Olive Island view; keep as the Cape Bauer/Whistling Rocks coast, not as a vehicle route (rules 1-3).
objection: A drive, not a single place; may duplicate other Streaky Bay features.

name: Westall Way Loop
reason: Tourism board lists a scenic coastal drive near Streaky Bay; its page was empty, so no named sights found. Needs a source naming stops.
objection: For: coastal granite and bays loop. Against: a drive with no detail in sources.

name: Swim with the Tuna
reason: Operator: a tuna-farm swim tour, not a place (COVERAGE: a tour is not a spot).
objection: Wikivoyage names it as a Port Lincoln experience.

name: Neptune Islands
reason: Island conservation park off Port Lincoln named by NPWS and Wikivoyage region; no landing, seen only from operator boats (cage diving).
objection: For: the place the shark tours go to. Against: unlandable, reached only via tour.

name: Thorny Passage Marine Park
reason: Offshore marine park area with no visitor point or thing to see (rule 2).
objection: Whales and sea lions occur there.

name: Yangie Bay
reason: Parks page: 2WD-accessible bay in Coffin Bay NP for canoeing, picnics and a coastal bushwalk (rules 1-3).
objection: Part of Coffin Bay National Park.

name: Yangie Lookout Walk
reason: duplicate of Yangie Bay: walk from the same bay, same source.
objection: A separate named walk.

name: Golden Island Lookout
reason: Parks page names the sealed-road Golden Island lookout with island views; one source, short visit.
objection: For: named lookout reachable by sedan. Against: a short lookout in the park.

name: Gunyah Beach
reason: 4WD-only northern beach in Coffin Bay NP; one generic parks mention (rules 1/3).
objection: Remote beaches appeal to anglers and surfers.

name: Almonta Beach
reason: Surf coast beach in Coffin Bay NP named on the parks page; 4WD in part, one source.
objection: For: well-known surf beach. Against: park-page mention only.

name: Sensation Beach
reason: Campground beach in Coffin Bay NP; one generic parks mention (rule 3).
objection: Part of the northern beaches draw.
